ei.title: 10번: The Hidden Costs of New Technology
ei.subject: 빠른독해바른독해_구문독해_2024

fullPassage: Although new technologies often seem to save us time and money, these savings vanish into thin air when we do a thorough cost analysis. For example, when email was first introduced, it changed the way we communicate. Whatever the message is and however long it may be, you can quickly type it out and send it anywhere for free. But there are other factors that must be considered. Spam emails need to be filtered out, and we all receive many messages that are unimportant but still must be read. This can be a time-consuming process. And when calculating the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your computer and smartphone, as well as the time it takes for your software to update. Roughly, it can be estimated that each email you send costs you one dollar, which is as much as an old-fashioned letter.

questions.passage: Although new technologies often seem to (A)[waste / save] us time and money, these savings vanish into thin air when we do a thorough cost analysis. For example, when email was first introduced, it changed the way we communicate. Whatever the message is and however long it may be, you can quickly type it out and send it anywhere for free. But there are other factors that must be considered. Spam emails need to be (B)[filtered / gathered] out, and we all receive many messages that are unimportant but still must be read. This can be a time-consuming process. And when calculating the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your computer and smartphone, as well as the time it takes for your software to (C)[update / delete]. Roughly, it can be estimated that each email you send costs you one dollar, which is as much as an old-fashioned letter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) save=아끼다 / waste=낭비하다 (B) filtered=걸러진 / gathered=모아진 (C) update=업데이트하다 / delete=삭제하다
det.analysis:
(A) 기술이 시간과 돈을 '아껴 주는(save)' 것처럼 보인다는 흐름이에요. waste(낭비하다)는 반대라 어색해요.

(B) 스팸 메일은 받은 편지함에서 '걸러내(filtered out)' 없애야 하죠. gathered(모으다)는 반대예요.

(C) 소프트웨어를 '업데이트하는(update)' 데 시간이 든다는 뜻이에요. delete(삭제)는 문맥에 안 맞아요.

따라서 save — filtered — update 조합이 정답이에요. ← 정답
det.tip: 각 자리의 원래 단어: save(아끼다), filtered(걸러진), update(갱신하다)

questions.passage: Although new technologies often seem to save us time and money, these savings vanish into thin air when we do a thorough cost analysis. For example, when email was first introduced, it changed the way we communicate. Whatever the message is and however long it may be, you can quickly type it out and send it anywhere for free. But there are other factors that must be (A)[ignored / considered]. Spam emails need to be filtered out, and we all receive many messages that are (B)[unimportant / urgent] but still must be read. This can be a time-consuming process. And when calculating the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your computer and smartphone, as well as the time it takes for your software to update. Roughly, it can be (C)[estimated / proven] that each email you send costs you one dollar, which is as much as an old-fashioned letter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) considered=고려된 / ignored=무시된 (B) unimportant=중요하지 않은 / urgent=긴급한 (C) estimated=추정된 / proven=증명된
det.analysis:
(A) '고려되어야(considered) 하는 다른 요인들이 있다'는 흐름이에요. ignored(무시된)는 반대예요.

(B) '중요하지 않은(unimportant) 메시지도 여전히 읽어야 한다'는 대비예요. urgent(긴급한)면 읽는 게 당연해 대비가 안 돼요.

(C) '이메일 한 통이 1달러라고 추정될(estimated) 수 있다'는 뜻이에요. proven(증명된)은 지나치게 단정적이에요.

따라서 considered — unimportant — estimated 조합이 정답이에요. ← 정답
det.tip: 각 자리의 원래 단어: considered(고려된), unimportant(사소한), estimated(추정된)

questions.passage: Although new technologies often seem to save us time and money, these savings vanish into thin air when we do a (A)[careless / thorough] cost analysis. For example, when email was first introduced, it changed the way we (B)[communicate / compete]. Whatever the message is and however long it may be, you can quickly type it out and send it anywhere for free. But there are other factors that must be considered. Spam emails need to be filtered out, and we all receive many messages that are unimportant but still must be read. This can be a time-consuming process. And when calculating the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your computer and smartphone, as well as the time it takes for your software to update. Roughly, it can be estimated that each email you send costs you one dollar, which is as much as an (C)[old-fashioned / brand-new] letter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) thorough=철저한 / careless=부주의한 (B) communicate=의사소통하다 / compete=경쟁하다 (C) old-fashioned=구식의 / brand-new=완전 새것의
det.analysis:
(A) '철저한(thorough) 비용 분석'을 하면 절감액이 사라진다는 흐름이에요. careless(부주의한)는 반대예요.

(B) '이메일이 우리가 소통하는(communicate) 방식을 바꿨다'는 뜻이에요. compete(경쟁하다)는 문맥에 안 맞아요.

(C) 이메일 비용이 '구식(old-fashioned) 편지'만큼 든다는 대비예요. brand-new(완전 새것)는 대비가 성립하지 않아요.

따라서 thorough — communicate — old-fashioned 조합이 정답이에요. ← 정답
det.tip: 각 자리의 원래 단어: thorough(철저한), communicate(소통하다), old-fashioned(구식의)

questions.passage: Although new technologies often seem to ①<u>save</u> us time and money, these savings vanish into thin air when we do a thorough cost analysis. For example, when email was first introduced, it changed the way we communicate. Whatever the message is and however long it may be, you can quickly type it out and send it anywhere for free. But there are other factors that must be considered. Spam emails need to be filtered out, and we all receive many messages that are ②<u>important</u> but still must be read. This can be a time-consuming process. And when calculating the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your ③<u>computer</u> and smartphone, as well as the time it takes for your software to update. Roughly, it can be estimated that each email you send costs you one dollar, which is as much as an ④<u>old-fashioned</u> letter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① save=아끼다 ② important→unimportant(중요하지 않은) ③ computer=컴퓨터 ④ old-fashioned=구식의
det.analysis:
① save: '시간과 돈을 아껴 주는(save) 것처럼 보인다' — 적절해요.

② important: '중요한(important) 메시지지만 여전히 읽어야 한다'는 앞뒤가 어색해요. 중요하면 읽는 게 당연하니까요. 원문은 '중요하지 않은(unimportant)' 메시지도 읽어야 한다는 대비라 unimportant가 맞아요. ← 여기가 정답

③ computer: '컴퓨터(computer)와 스마트폰의 비용' — 적절해요.

④ old-fashioned: '구식(old-fashioned) 편지만큼' — 적절해요.
det.tip: '~하지 않은 것도 …해야 한다'는 대비 → unimportant(사소한). important(중요한)면 대비가 안 됨

questions.passage: Although new technologies often seem to ①<u>waste</u> us time and money, these savings vanish into thin air when we do a thorough cost analysis. For example, when email was first introduced, it changed the way we ②<u>communicate</u>. Whatever the message is and however long it may be, you can quickly type it out and send it anywhere for free. But there are other factors that must be considered. Spam emails need to be ③<u>filtered</u> out, and we all receive many messages that are unimportant but still must be read. This can be a time-consuming process. And when calculating the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your computer and smartphone, as well as the time it takes for your software to update. Roughly, it can be estimated that each email you send costs you one dollar, which is as much as an old-fashioned ④<u>letter</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① waste→save(아끼다) ② communicate=소통하다 ③ filtered=걸러진 ④ letter=편지
det.analysis:
① waste: '기술이 시간과 돈을 낭비하는(waste) 것처럼 보인다'? 첫 문장은 기술이 겉보기에 시간·돈을 '아껴 주는(save)' 것처럼 보인다는 흐름이라 waste는 반대예요. ← 여기가 정답

② communicate: '우리가 소통하는(communicate) 방식을 바꿨다' — 적절해요.

③ filtered: '스팸 메일은 걸러내져야(filtered out) 한다' — 적절해요.

④ letter: '구식 편지(letter)만큼' — 적절해요.
det.tip: 겉보기엔 기술이 시간·돈을 save(아껴 준다). waste(낭비)는 정반대

questions.passage: Although new technologies often seem to save us time and money, these savings vanish into thin air when we do a ①<u>thorough</u> cost analysis. For example, when email was first ②<u>introduced</u>, it changed the way we communicate. Whatever the message is and however long it may be, you can quickly type it out and send it anywhere for free. But there are other factors that must be considered. Spam emails need to be filtered out, and we all receive many messages that are unimportant but still must be read. This can be a ③<u>time-consuming</u> process. And when calculating the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your computer and smartphone, as well as the time it takes for your software to update. Roughly, it can be ④<u>denied</u> that each email you send costs you one dollar, which is as much as an old-fashioned letter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① thorough=철저한 ② introduced=도입된 ③ time-consuming=시간이 걸리는 ④ denied→estimated(추정된)
det.analysis:
① thorough: '철저한(thorough) 비용 분석' — 적절해요.

② introduced: '이메일이 처음 도입되었을(introduced) 때' — 적절해요.

③ time-consuming: '시간을 잡아먹는(time-consuming) 과정' — 적절해요.

④ denied: '이메일 한 통이 1달러라고 부정될(denied) 수 있다'? 글은 이메일에도 숨은 비용이 든다고 추정하는 내용이라, denied가 아니라 '추정될(estimated)'이 맞아요. ← 여기가 정답
det.tip: 숨은 비용을 계산해 '추정한다(estimated)'. denied(부정하다)는 문맥과 반대

For example, when email was first introduced, it changed the way we communicate. Whatever the message is and however long it may be, you can quickly type it out and send it anywhere for free. But there are other factors that must be considered. Spam emails need to be filtered out, and we all receive many messages that are unimportant but still must be read. This can be a time-consuming process. And when calculating the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your computer and smartphone, as well as the time it takes for your software to update. Roughly, it can be estimated that each email you send costs you one dollar, which is as much as an old-fashioned letter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: report=보고서 / increase=증가 / analysis=분석 / payment=지불
det.analysis:
빈칸은 '철저한 비용 ______를 할 때'예요. 비용을 자세히 따져 보는 것을 뜻하니 '분석(analysis)'이 맞아요.

① report(보고서): 비용을 '하다(do)'와 어울리지 않아요.

② increase(증가): 비용 증가를 '한다'는 어색해요.

③ analysis(분석): '비용 분석을 하다(do a cost analysis)'로 자연스러워요. ← 정답

④ payment(지불): 앞의 do와 의미가 맞지 않아요.
det.tip: do a thorough cost ______ = 철저한 비용 분석을 하다 → analysis

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: signals=신호 / factors=요인 / benefits=이익 / savings=절감액
det.analysis:
빈칸은 '고려되어야 할 다른 ______이 있다'예요. 비용을 따질 때 함께 봐야 할 '요인(factors)'을 말해요.

① signals(신호): 고려 대상으로 어색해요.

② factors(요인): '고려되어야 할 다른 요인들'로 자연스러워요. ← 정답

③ benefits(이익): 뒤에 스팸·시간 등 부담 요소가 나오므로 이익은 안 맞아요.

④ savings(절감액): 절감액은 앞에서 사라진다고 했으므로 문맥과 어긋나요.
det.tip: other ______ that must be considered = 고려해야 할 다른 요인들 → factors

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: reward=보상 / holiday=휴일 / discount=할인 / process=과정
det.analysis:
빈칸은 '이것은 시간을 잡아먹는 ______일 수 있다'예요. 스팸을 걸러내고 불필요한 메일까지 읽는 '일/과정(process)'을 가리켜요.

① reward(보상): 시간을 잡아먹는 '보상'은 어색해요.

② holiday(휴일): 문맥과 무관해요.

③ discount(할인): 문맥과 무관해요.

④ process(과정): '시간이 많이 드는 과정'으로 자연스러워요. ← 정답
det.tip: time-consuming ______ = 시간이 많이 드는 과정 → process

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 quickly와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: quickly=빠르게 / rapidly=신속하게 / slowly=느리게 / rarely=드물게 / quietly=조용히
det.analysis:
① rapidly(신속하게): quickly와 같은 '빠르게'라는 뜻이에요. ← 정답

② slowly(느리게): quickly의 반대예요.

③ rarely(드물게): 빈도를 말해 의미가 달라요.

④ quietly(조용히): 소리에 대한 말이라 의미가 달라요.
det.tip: quickly = 빠르게 ≒ rapidly(신속하게)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 thorough와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: thorough=철저한 / quick=빠른 / partial=부분적인 / complete=완전한, 철저한 / cheap=값싼
det.analysis:
① quick(빠른): 속도를 말해 '철저함'과 달라요.

② partial(부분적인): 철저한과 반대예요.

③ complete(완전한, 빠짐없는): 하나도 빠뜨리지 않고 자세히 하는 thorough와 뜻이 가까워요. ← 정답

④ cheap(값싼): 가격을 말해 의미가 달라요.
det.tip: thorough = 철저한, 빠짐없는 ≒ complete(완전한)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 estimated와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: estimated=추정된 / proven=증명된 / calculated=계산된 / doubted=의심받은 / increased=증가된
det.analysis:
① proven(증명된): 확실히 입증한다는 뜻이라 '어림잡아 추정'하는 estimated보다 강해요.

② calculated(계산된, 어림한): 수치를 따져 어림잡는다는 점에서 estimated와 뜻이 가까워요. ← 정답

③ doubted(의심받은): 의미가 전혀 달라요.

④ increased(증가된): 양의 변화를 말해 달라요.
det.tip: estimate = 추정하다, 어림잡다 ≒ calculate(계산하다/어림하다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 unimportant와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: unimportant=중요하지 않은 / significant=중요한 / trivial=사소한 / silent=조용한 / cheap=값싼
det.analysis:

③ silent(조용한): 소리에 대한 말이라 의미축이 달라요.

④ cheap(값싼): 가격에 대한 말이라 의미축이 달라요.
det.tip: unimportant(사소한) ↔ significant(중요한). trivial은 오히려 유의어

questions.passage: Although new technologies often seem to save us time and money, these savings vanish into thin air when we do a thorough cost analysis. For example, when email was first introduced, it changed the way we communicate. Whatever the message is and however long it may be, you can quickly type it out and send it anywhere for free. But there are other factors that must be considered. Spam emails need to be filtered out, and we all receive many messages that are unimportant but still must be read. This can be a time-consuming process. And when calculating the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your computer and smartphone, as well as the time it takes for your software to update. Roughly, it can be estimated that each email you send costs you one dollar, which is as much as an <u>old-fashioned</u> letter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 old-fashioned와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: old-fashioned=구식의 / traditional=전통적인 / classic=고전적인 / expensive=비싼 / modern=현대적인
det.analysis:
① traditional(전통적인): old-fashioned와 비슷한 뜻이라 반대가 아니에요.

② classic(고전적인): 역시 옛것과 관련되어 반대가 아니에요.

③ expensive(비싼): 가격에 대한 말이라 의미축이 달라요.

④ modern(현대적인): old-fashioned(구식의)의 반대말이에요. ← 정답
det.tip: old-fashioned(구식) ↔ modern(현대적). traditional/classic은 오히려 유의어

questions.passage:
(A) Whatever the message is, you can quickly type it out and send it anywhere for <u>free</u>, without paying anything at all.

(B) After she finished all of her work early, she felt completely <u>free</u> and spent the whole afternoon relaxing in the park.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 free의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: free: (A) 무료의, 공짜의 (B) 자유로운, 얽매이지 않은
det.analysis:
(A) 'send it anywhere for free'는 '어디로든 무료로 보낸다'는 뜻이라 free = 무료의예요.

(B) 'she felt completely free'는 할 일을 다 끝내고 '자유로운/홀가분한' 기분을 느꼈다는 뜻이라 free = 자유로운이에요.

① (A) 무료의 (B) 자유로운: 두 문맥에 정확히 맞아요. ← 정답

② (A) 자유로운 (B) 무료의: 두 자리가 뒤바뀌었어요.

③ 둘 다 무료의: (B)가 안 맞아요.

④ 둘 다 자유로운: (A)가 안 맞아요.
det.tip: free의 다의어: for free = 무료로(값이 없음) vs feel free = 자유로운(얽매이지 않은)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "to disappear suddenly and completely"

det.korean: gather=모으다 / vanish=사라지다 / increase=증가하다 / appear=나타나다
det.analysis:
정의는 '갑자기 그리고 완전히 사라지다'예요.

① gather(모으다): 흩어진 것을 모으는 것이라 반대예요.

② vanish(사라지다): '흔적도 없이 갑자기 사라지다'라는 뜻과 정확히 맞아요. ← 정답

③ increase(증가하다): 양이 느는 것이라 무관해요.

④ appear(나타나다): vanish의 반대말이에요.
det.tip: disappear suddenly and completely = 갑자기 완전히 사라지다 → vanish

questions.passage: For example, when email was first __________ (introduce), it changed the way we communicate.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: introduce(도입하다) → introduced (be + 과거분사 수동태). 이메일이 '도입된' 것
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞에 'was first'가 있어요. 이메일은 사람에 의해 '도입되는' 대상이므로 수동태 be + 과거분사(p.p.)를 써야 해요. introduce의 과거분사는 introduced예요.

따라서 'email was first introduced' = '이메일이 처음 도입되었다'가 돼요.
det.tip: was + ______ → 수동태(be + p.p.) → introduced

questions.passage: And when __________ (calculate) the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your computer and smartphone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: calculate(계산하다) → calculating (접속사 when + 분사구문, 주어 생략 시 -ing)
det.analysis:
접속사 when 뒤에 주어 없이 동사가 바로 오면 분사구문이라 -ing 형태를 써요. 원래는 'when you calculate'인데 주어 you가 생략되고 동사가 calculating으로 바뀐 거예요.

따라서 'when calculating the cost savings' = '비용 절감액을 계산할 때'가 돼요.
det.tip: When + (주어 생략) + 동사 → 분사구문(-ing) → calculating

And when calculating the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your computer and smartphone, as well as the time it takes for your software to update. Roughly, it can be estimated that each email you send costs you one dollar, which is as much as an old-fashioned letter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: However=그러나 / In contrast=반대로 / For example=예를 들어 / As a result=결과적으로
det.analysis:
앞 문장은 '기술의 절감액이 사실은 사라진다'는 일반적인 주장이에요. 빈칸 뒤에서는 그 예로 '이메일'을 드니, 빈칸에는 '예를 들어(For example)'가 알맞아요.

① However(그러나): 앞뒤가 대조되지 않아요.

② In contrast(반대로): 예시를 드는 흐름이라 안 맞아요.

③ For example(예를 들어): 일반 주장 뒤에 구체적 예(이메일)를 드는 연결이라 딱 맞아요. ← 정답

④ As a result(결과적으로): 원인-결과 관계가 아니에요.
det.tip: 일반 주장 → 구체적 예시(이메일) 연결 = For example(예를 들어)

questions.passage: Although new technologies often seem to save us time and money, these savings vanish into thin air when we do a thorough cost analysis. For example, when email was first introduced, it changed the way we communicate. Whatever the message is and however long it may be, you can quickly type it out and send it anywhere for free. But there are other factors that must be considered. Spam emails need to be filtered out, and we all receive many messages that are unimportant but still must be read. This can be a time-consuming process. And when calculating the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your computer and smartphone, as well as the time it takes for your software to update. Roughly, it can be estimated that each email you send costs you one dollar, which is __________ an old-fashioned letter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: less than=~보다 적은 / more than=~보다 많은 / cheaper than=~보다 싼 / as much as=~만큼
det.analysis:
이 글의 핵심은 공짜처럼 보이는 이메일도 사실은 비용이 든다는 거예요. 이메일 한 통이 1달러인데, 이는 옛날 편지 '만큼(as much as)' 든다는 대비로 마무리돼요.

① less than(~보다 적은): 이메일이 더 싸다는 뜻이 되어 글의 주장과 반대예요.

② more than(~보다 많은): 편지보다 비싸다는 근거는 없어요.

③ cheaper than(~보다 싼): 역시 이메일이 싸다는 뜻이라 주장과 반대예요.

④ as much as(~만큼): '옛날 편지만큼 든다'는 대비로 글의 결론과 딱 맞아요. ← 정답
det.tip: 공짜 같던 이메일이 사실은 옛날 편지'만큼' 비쌈 → as much as(~만큼)
